newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai King calls for unity in next government.
newsitem.headline: Thai King calls for unity in next government.

text.p: Thailand's King Bhumibol Adulyadej opened parliament on Saturday with a call to the nation's often-fractious parties to work together in the people's best interest.

King Bhumibol, the world's longest-reigning monarch, spoke as he officially opened the new session of parliament and began the process to appoint New Aspiration Party (NAP) leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh the country's 22nd prime minister.

"It is your direct burden and responsibility to work together and be united to perform to the best of your ability for the prosperity of the nation and the people," the king said in a brief five-minute speech.
"Any debate about the nation's problems in this parliament should be really made for the nation's and people's interest."
The house was then due to elect deputy NAP leader Wan Muhamad Nor Matha as parliament president, who is expected to nominate Chavalit as prime minister in the next day or two.

The NAP won a narrow two-seat victory over the Democrat Party in a general election on November 17. It has formed a six-party coalition which has a comfortable majority of 221 seats in the 393-seat parliament.
The party ousted the 14-month old trouble-plagued coalition of Chart Thai leader Banharn Silpa-archa.
The next step in the formation of the new government is for Wan Muhamed to formally nominate Chavalit as prime minister and seek royal approval for the nomination.

Analysts and politicians say this is expected to take place by Monday, in time for Chavalit to be the new leader so he can welcome U.S. president Bill Clinton who arrives in Bangkok late on Monday for a brief state visit to Thailand.
Chavalit has been in intense negotiations with his coalition partners over the makeup of the cabinet since his election victory last Sunday.

The main delay has stemmed from differences over how to share out economic portfolios, coalition sources said. The coalition has given the economy top priority and vowed to appoint a qualified economic team to improve a slowing economy.
Chavalit said on Thursday he expects to complete the cabinet next week.
